Thanks — short update from my side: I've populated tab B (Model Catalog & Provenance) with the following patterns for each model entry:

- Declared upstream source: package name / repo URL and commit sha when available (we include both when model is from a VCS or checkpoint repo).
- Packaging provenance: where we verified the artifact (Redwood internal registry vs third-party storage).
- Training data origin: summarized (public corpus / licensed dataset / partner dataset).
- Pinning recommendation (per-model): enterprise pin to exact model artifact (commit sha or wheel digest) OR pin to Redwood-managed snapshot tag with explicit update window.

A couple of notes that might be helpful for your reviewers:
- For open models we record the SPDX or declared license text and include a link to the source release; when license files are missing we flag for legal review.
- For models we host in Redwood Dedicated/Private, enterprise customers can opt for immutable pinning (we persist an immutable artifact id and do not auto-update) or managed pinning (Redwood will deliver security/patch updates with notice and explicit migration windows).

I uploaded the updated workbook to the SharePoint link and added row-level comments where we need DataCorp's confirmation (notably: third-party dataset attributions for Model X and binary redistribution for Model Y).

Let me know if you want me on the call tomorrow; otherwise I'll continue finishing tab D.

—Marissa
